title: Control Room Weeknote: Hotfix Lifecycle & Change Summary
content:
Purpose
Summary notes from this week’s control-room/ops cadence focused on hotfix lifecycle, last weekend’s release ripple, canary observations, and a prioritized action list for next window. This doc is the canonical short-form log for the release engineering on-call and SRE handoffs.

Meeting metadata
- Date: 2025-11-03 weekly control-room sync (follow-ups 2025-11-07)
- Time: 09:00–09:45 PT
- Facilitator: Maya Patel (release lead)
- Attendees: Maya Patel, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nambiar, Zoe Chen, Arjun Rao, Samir Gupta (SRE), Claire Duan (product-hosted-api)
- Slack channel: #release-control (pinned: runbook link, incident notes)

Agenda
1) Quick recap: last weekend’s rollout and observed regressions
2) Hotfix lifecycle decisions for REDINF-2147
3) Canary metric review and automatic rollback thresholds
4) Change log alignment for this train and dependent ops tasks
5) Action items and owners

Recap / context
- Saturday night release (train v2025.11.01) deployed hosted-api and serving-runtime binaries across two US regions and one EU region. The deployment included: a minor serving-runtime kernel selection tweak to improve long-sequence throughput, updated autoscaler bounds for Dedicated clusters, and a config change to prefix cache TTL for KV cache.
- Post-deploy there were intermittent 5xx spikes for the hosted-api route /v1/generate in us-west-2 between 02:12–02:47 UTC (peak error rate: 3.8%). Affected customers: small number of low-latency PLG tests; no Dedicated customers on reserved capacity were impacted.
- Root cause (tentative): increased KV cache miss storm during rolling rollout combined with an aggressive autoscaler cooldown on a subset of workers leading to transient queueing and tokenization timeouts on the binary that uses a new attention kernel (see GH PR 987).

Hotfix / lifecycle decision (REDINF-2147)
- Ticket: REDINF-2147 - tokenization timeouts under rollout
- Priority: P1 (customer-impacting but contained)
- Decision: deploy targeted hotfix 2025.11.01-hotfix1 to us-west-2 canary nodes only, with staged expansion if canary is clean. Hotfix includes: revert kernel selector to v2.3 fallback path for sequences >1024, add short-term tokenization timeout bump from 6s->10s, and enable KV cache warmup on new replicas.
- Hotfix window: immediate canary (today 13:00 PT), 30m canary evaluation, then staged to remaining nodes in us-west-2 in 3 waves with 20m evaluation per wave. If canary passes metrics, schedule EU expansion tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

Canary metrics & rollback criteria
- Primary metrics to observe (canary):
  * p95 request latency for /v1/generate (target: <= 420ms)
  * 5xx error rate (target: <= 0.5%)
  * tokenization-timeout count (should trend to 0)
  * KV cache hit ratio (baseline: 82%)
- Canary thresholds for automatic rollback: if 5xx >= 1% sustained for 5 minutes OR p95 increases >25% over baseline for 10 minutes OR tokenization-timeout count >3 in 10 minutes -> automatic rollback.
- Manual rollback triggers: any sign of cascading increase in client retries or unbounded queue length on worker (SRE judgement).

Observed canary snapshot (post-hotfix canary window 13:00–13:40 PT)
- p95 latency: 390ms -> improved vs pre-hotfix 460ms
- 5xx error rate: 0.2% -> back to baseline
- tokenization-timeouts: 0 observed in window
- KV cache hit ratio: 79% -> small dip but expected during warmup
- Verdict: canary green; proceed with staged expansion.

Change log summary (for release notes and internal rollouts)
- Release train v2025.11.01-hotfix1 (applied 2025-11-03):
  * Reverted kernel selector for long sequences to fallback path (serving-runtime)
  * Tokenization timeout extended for stability (short-term only)
  * KV cache warmup enabled on new replicas to prevent cold-miss storms
  * Autoscaler cooldown adjustments reverted for Dedicated pool A
- Impacted services: hosted-api (/v1/generate), serving-runtime, autoscaler-controller (config only).
- Backwards compat: no changes to public API surface or model routing; no client action required.

Outstanding risks & mitigations
- Risk: fallback kernel increases CPU cycles on some instance types (esp. older T4/GPU types), could raise cost/thermal pressure. Mitigation: monitor per-instance GPU utilization and cap hotfix expansion if utilization > 85% on any node.
- Risk: KV cache warmup increases short-lived memory pressure. Mitigation: limit parallel warmups to 5 nodes at a time; observe OOM metrics for 2 hours post-rollout.
- Risk: change in autoscaler behavior might oscillate in low-traffic windows. Mitigation: revert cooldowns for Dedicated pool A was included in hotfix.

Action items (owner — due date — status)
- Maya Patel — 2025-11-05 — verify rollout sequencing doc and update runbook for canary thresholds (status: in_progress)
- Diego Alvarez — 2025-11-04 — add per-instance GPU utilization alert and dashboard (status: todo) — DASH: infra/gpu-utilization-hotfix
- Priya Nambiar — 2025-11-06 — follow up with model-onboarding team to confirm kernel selector test coverage for long-sequence models (status: todo) — linked: GitHub PR 987
- Zoe Chen — 2025-11-05 — draft customer-facing incident summary and notify impacted PLG users (status: todo)
- Arjun Rao — 2025-11-07 — post-mortem draft (include timeline, detection, mitigation, follow-ups) (status: todo) — JIRA:REDINF-2201

Follow-up items / questions
- Is the autoscaler config change documented in product-hosted-api release notes? (Claire to confirm).
- Consider adding a pre-rollout KV cache warmup job to future trains to avoid similar storms. Proposal: scheduled warmup job that seeds popular prefixes for 15m before traffic switch. (Priya to prototype).

Notes to on-call for next 48h
- Watch: p95 latency, 5xx rate, tokenization timeout counter, per-instance GPU util.
- If errors resurface in a different region, treat as independent incident; do not auto-expand hotfix without separate canary.
- For Dedicated customers: notify account owners proactively if we need to extend hotfix to reserved clusters.

Next meetings
- Short follow-up sync: 2025-11-04 08:00 PT (15m) — verify dashboards and alerts are in place.
- Post-mortem working session: 2025-11-07 11:00 PT (1h) — all owners expected.
